title: The deposit is a price, not a formality
subtitle: The cheaper of two identical fares is usually the one you cannot walk away from.

text: A non-refundable deposit is a discount you pay for in advance.
sub: You are selling the line certainty about your cabin. That is worth something, and they price it. The question is whether you had certainty to sell.

title: Four dates to write down at booking

items.head: Deposit due
items.body: Usually days after booking, not weeks. Miss it and the cabin releases without ceremony.

items.head: Last day to reprice
items.body: In practice, before final payment. This is the window in which a fare drop is still useful to you.

items.head: Final payment
items.body: The cliff edge. After it the money is committed and cancellation penalties begin climbing.

items.head: Insurance cut-off
items.body: Some cover, particularly pre-existing conditions, must be bought within days of the deposit.

quote: Take the non-refundable deposit when the dates are certain. Not when the fare is tempting.

text: Choose the deposit that matches your life, not the headline.
sub: Fixed dates and settled health: take the lower fare. A parent unwell, a business mid-sale, a passport near expiry: pay for the exit and sleep.

title: Save this for the day you put a deposit down
body: Or send me the sailing and I'll tell you which deposit structure I'd take on it, and why.
